newsitem.title: UK: Next profits up 27 percent, shares slip.
newsitem.headline: Next profits up 27 percent, shares slip.

text.p: British fashion chain Next Plc Wednesday unveiled a sharp rise in first half profits, but its stock fell on fears that current sales may have lagged an upturn in consumer spending.
Pretax profits in the first half were nearly 27 percent higher at 56 million pounds ($87 million) and at the top of market expectations.
But disappointment with sales growth in the second half dampened enthusiasm for the results and hit the shares, which fell 23.5 pence (37 cents)to 576.5 pence ($9.00).

Next stores saw sales rise by 23 percent on selling space that was 5 percent up on the previous year. Next Directory, the mail order business, boosted sales by 23 percent and operating profit by 42 percent.
Total sales sales rose to 406.4 million pounds ($635 million) from 333.3 million ($521 million).
